transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. We have a significant matter to address today — the customer class action arising from the account information exposure through our software vendor's compromised credentials. As we all know, the complaint seeks damages, injunctive relief, and public disclosure of the incident, and we have not yet sent our formal coverage tender or selected litigation counsel. This meeting is where we finalize and approve the response package, so we need to move efficiently. I'd like to go through the round-robin review with each of the four counsel functions — insurance, claims, client-relations, and conflicts — so we can get your formal findings on the record. Once all four have disclosed, I'll make the approval decision in-session. Let's begin with insurance counsel. What do you have for us?

transcript.text: Thank you, Elena. I'm ready to present my conflicts findings when we reach my turn in the round-robin. I have a material conflict issue that will affect our counsel selection, and I'll need to place it formally on the record at that point.

transcript.text: Thank you, Elena. I have a critical coverage finding that needs to go on the record. This morning I reviewed the cyber policy's vendor-breach endorsement, which I received shortly before this meeting. I confirmed that this claim qualifies for coverage only if our formal tender identifies the event as a vendor-breach privacy claim. That specific characterization in the tender is a condition for coverage. I have not yet circulated the endorsement analysis because the carrier's coverage file came in right before we convened, but I'm placing this finding on the record now so it informs the response package we're approving today.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to formally enter something into the committee record. Yesterday I obtained the carrier's written claims note, which approves defense-funded mediation first and settlement authority of exactly $900,000, provided the company follows that sequence. I have not uploaded the note to the claims system yet because it was undergoing its weekly maintenance window, but given our recordkeeping procedure, I'm placing these operative terms on the record now before we proceed to approval.

transcript.text: Before we proceed further, I need to formally disclose something for the committee record. This instruction has not yet been added to the claim plan, but it directly affects the response package we're being asked to approve today — particularly given that the complaint seeks public disclosure of the incident. I'm placing this on the record now as a client-relations finding so it can be incorporated before any approval decision.

The response package must reflect the appointment of independent defense counsel rather than the insurer's panel firm.
